questions.question: A trader marks his goods 50% above cost price and then allows two successive discounts of 10% and 20%. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution: SP = CP × 1.5 × 0.9 × 0.8 = 1.08 × CP, so the profit is 8%.

questions.question: Ravi's income rises by 20% and his expenditure rises by 10%. As a result, his savings rise by 50%. What percentage of his original income did he originally save?
questions.solution: Let income = 100 and expenditure = E. New savings: 120 − 1.1E = 1.5(100 − E) ⇒ 0.4E = 30 ⇒ E = 75. Savings = 25% of income.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells an article at a 20% profit. Had he bought it for 10% less and sold it for ₹18 less, his profit would have been 25%. What is the cost price (in ₹)?

In a two-candidate election, 10% of registered voters did not vote and 10% of the votes cast were invalid. The winner got 54% of the valid votes and won by 1,620 votes. How many registered voters were there?
questions.solution: Valid votes = 0.9 × 0.9 × N = 0.81N. The margin is 54% − 46% = 8% of valid votes: 0.08 × 0.81N = 0.0648N = 1620 ⇒ N = 25,000.

questions.question: Two cars start at the same time from P and Q and drive towards each other. After they meet, the car from P takes 4 hours to reach Q and the car from Q takes 9 hours to reach P. If the car from P travels at 45 km/h, what is the distance PQ (in km)?
questions.solution: If the meeting happens after t hours: t² = 4 × 9 ⇒ t = 6 h, and speed ratio = √(9/4) = 3 : 2, so the other car does 30 km/h. PQ = (45 + 30) × 6 = 450 km. Check: P-car covers 270 km before meeting, then the remaining 180 km at 45 km/h = 4 h ✓.

questions.question: A train passes a man walking at 3 km/h in the same direction in 10 seconds, and a man walking at 6 km/h towards it in 8 seconds. What is the length of the train?

A and B start together from the same point on a 1,200 m circular track and run in the same direction at 5 m/s and 7 m/s. After how many seconds will they first be together at the starting point again?
questions.solution: A completes a lap every 240 s and B every 1200/7 s. Both are at the start at times that are multiples of both: 240a = 1200b/7 ⇒ 7a = 5b, smallest a = 5 ⇒ 1,200 s. (They do meet at 600 s too, but halfway round the track, not at the start.)

questions.question: A boat goes 30 km upstream and 44 km downstream in 10 hours. It goes 40 km upstream and 55 km downstream in 13 hours. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.solution: Let u = 1/upstream speed and d = 1/downstream speed: 30u + 44d = 10 and 40u + 55d = 13. Solving gives u = 1/5 and d = 1/11, so the upstream speed is 5 and the downstream speed 11. Stream = (11 − 5)/2 = 3 km/h.

questions.question: Walking at 5 km/h, Meera reaches office 6 minutes late. Walking at 6 km/h, she reaches 4 minutes early. How far is her office?
questions.solution: The time difference is 10 min = 1/6 h. d/5 − d/6 = 1/6 ⇒ d/30 = 1/6 ⇒ d = 5 km.

questions.question: A and B together can finish a job in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. In how many days can A alone finish it?
12 men or 18 women can finish a piece of work in 14 days. How many days will 8 men and 16 women take to finish it?
questions.solution: 1 man = 18/12 = 1.5 women. 8 men + 16 women = 28 women. Work = 18 × 14 = 252 woman-days ⇒ 252/28 = 9 days.

questions.question: Pipes A and B fill a tank in 20 and 30 minutes respectively, and pipe C empties it in 15 minutes. All three are opened on an empty tank, and C is closed after 10 minutes. How many minutes in total does it take to fill the tank?
questions.solution: With all three open: 1/20 + 1/30 − 1/15 = 1/60 per minute, so 10 minutes fill 1/6. The remaining 5/6 at A + B = 1/12 per minute takes 10 minutes. Total = 20 minutes.

questions.question: A is twice as efficient as B, and together they finish a job in 14 days. How many days would A alone take?
questions.solution: If B does b per day, A does 2b, so 3b = 1/14 ⇒ b = 1/42 and A = 1/21 ⇒ 21 days.

questions.question: A 60-litre mixture of milk and water contains 20% water. How many litres of water must be added so that water becomes 25% of the new mixture?
questions.solution: Milk = 48 L and stays fixed. For 75% milk, total = 48/0.75 = 64 L, so add 4 L of water.

questions.question: A vessel contains 80 litres of pure wine. 8 litres are taken out and replaced with water, and this is done three times in all. How much wine is left?
questions.solution: Each operation keeps 72/80 = 0.9 of the wine. Wine left = 80 × 0.9³ = 58.32 L.

questions.question: Alloy X has copper and zinc in the ratio 3 : 2, and alloy Y has them in the ratio 1 : 3. In what ratio (X : Y) must they be mixed to get an alloy with equal amounts of copper and zinc?
questions.solution: Copper fraction: X = 0.6, Y = 0.25, target 0.5. By alligation, X : Y = (0.5 − 0.25) : (0.6 − 0.5) = 0.25 : 0.1 = 5 : 2.

questions.question: A sum grows to ₹13,310 in 3 years and to ₹14,641 in 4 years at compound interest (compounded annually). What is the principal?
The difference between compound and simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 10% per annum is ₹93. What is the sum?
Riya deposits ₹1,000 at the start of each year for 2 years in an account paying 10% per annum compounded annually. What is the balance (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
questions.solution: The first deposit grows for 2 years: 1000 × 1.21 = 1210. The second grows for 1 year: 1000 × 1.1 = 1100. Total = ₹2,310.

questions.question: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 7. Six years ago they were in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the sum of their present ages?
questions.solution: (5k − 6)/(7k − 6) = 2/3 ⇒ 15k − 18 = 14k − 12 ⇒ k = 6. The ages are 30 and 42, so the sum is 72.

questions.question: A bag has ₹1, 50-paise and 25-paise coins in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4 by number, worth ₹216 in total. How many 50-paise coins are there?
questions.solution: Value per set of (2, 3, 4) coins = 2 + 1.5 + 1 = ₹4.5. Sets = 216/4.5 = 48. 50-paise coins = 3 × 48 = 144.

questions.question: x varies directly as y² and inversely as z. When y = 2 and z = 3, x = 12. Find x when y = 4 and z = 8.
The roots of x² − px + 12 = 0 differ by 1, and p > 0. What is p?
questions.solution: (r₁ − r₂)² = (r₁ + r₂)² − 4r₁r₂ = p² − 48 = 1 ⇒ p = 7. (The roots are 3 and 4.)

questions.question: For how many integer values of k does x² + kx + 16 = 0 have no real roots?
questions.solution: No real roots ⇔ discriminant < 0 ⇔ k² < 64 ⇔ −8 < k < 8. The integers −7 to 7 make 15 values.

questions.question: If α and β are the roots of x² − 5x + 3 = 0, what is α³ + β³?
questions.solution: α + β = 5 and αβ = 3. α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β) = 125 − 45 = 80.

questions.question: How many ordered pairs of positive integers (x, y) satisfy 3x + 5y = 100?
questions.solution: 100 − 5y must be a positive multiple of 3. That needs y ≡ 2 (mod 3) with 5y < 100: y = 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, giving 6 pairs (e.g. y = 2, x = 30; y = 17, x = 5).

questions.question: The digits of a two-digit number add up to 9. Reversing the digits increases the number by 27. What is the number?
questions.solution: Let the number be 10a + b with a + b = 9. Reversing adds 9(b − a) = 27 ⇒ b − a = 3. So a = 3, b = 6, and the number is 36.

questions.question: How many integers x satisfy |x − 3| + |x + 2| < 9?
questions.solution: For −2 ≤ x ≤ 3 the sum is always 5 (6 integers). For x > 3: 2x − 1 < 9 ⇒ x < 5, so x = 4. For x < −2: 1 − 2x < 9 ⇒ x > −4, so x = −3. The answer is x = −3 to 4, which is 8 integers.

questions.question: For which values of x is x² − 7x + 10 < 0?
questions.solution: x² − 7x + 10 = (x − 2)(x − 5) is negative strictly between its roots, so 2 < x < 5.

questions.question: What is the minimum value of (x² + 2x + 9)/(x + 1) for x > −1?
questions.solution: (x² + 2x + 9)/(x + 1) = (x + 1) + 8/(x + 1). By AM–GM this is at least 2√8 = 4√2, with equality when x + 1 = 2√2.

questions.question: f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = x² − 1. What is the sum of all real x for which f(g(x)) = g(f(x))?
questions.solution: f(g(x)) = 2x² + 1 and g(f(x)) = (2x + 3)² − 1 = 4x² + 12x + 8. Setting them equal gives 2x² + 12x + 7 = 0. The discriminant is 144 − 56 > 0, so both roots are real, and their sum is −12/2 = −6.

questions.question: f(x) + 2f(1/x) = 3x for every non-zero real x. What is f(2)?
What is the minimum value of f(x) = |x − 2| + |x − 5|?
questions.solution: The sum of distances from x to 2 and to 5 is smallest (= 5 − 2 = 3) for any x between 2 and 5.

questions.question: If log₂(log₃(log₂ x)) = 1, what is x?
questions.solution: log₃(log₂ x) = 2 ⇒ log₂ x = 9 ⇒ x = 2⁹ = 512.

questions.question: Given log₁₀ 2 = 0.3010, how many digits does 2⁵⁰ have?
questions.solution: log₁₀ 2⁵⁰ = 50 × 0.3010 = 15.05. The number of digits = ⌊15.05⌋ + 1 = 16.

questions.question: Solve log₂(x − 1) + log₂(x + 1) = 3.
questions.solution: log₂[(x − 1)(x + 1)] = 3 ⇒ x² − 1 = 8 ⇒ x = ±3. But x − 1 > 0 is needed for the log, so only x = 3 works.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 7¹⁰⁰ is divided by 13?
questions.solution: 7¹² ≡ 1 (mod 13) by Fermat's little theorem. 100 = 12 × 8 + 4, so 7¹⁰⁰ ≡ 7⁴ = 2401 = 13 × 184 + 9 ≡ 9.

questions.question: How many divisors of 2⁴ × 3³ × 5² are perfect squares?
questions.solution: A square divisor needs even exponents: 2 ∈ {0, 2, 4} (3 ways), 3 ∈ {0, 2} (2 ways), 5 ∈ {0, 2} (2 ways). 3 × 2 × 2 = 12.

questions.question: What is the sum of all positive divisors of 72?
What is the highest power of 3 that divides 100!?
What is the smallest number that leaves remainder 3 when divided by 5, 6 or 8, and is divisible by 9?
questions.solution: Such numbers are 120k + 3. We need 120k + 3 ≡ 0 (mod 9). 120 ≡ 3, so 3k + 3 ≡ 0 (mod 9) ⇒ k ≡ 2 (mod 3). Smallest k = 2 ⇒ 243.

questions.question: What are the last two digits of 3⁴⁰?
questions.solution: 3²⁰ ≡ 1 (mod 100) (Carmichael's λ(100) = 20; check 3¹⁰ = 59049 ≡ 49 and 49² = 2401 ≡ 01). So 3⁴⁰ ≡ 1 ⇒ last two digits 01.

questions.question: How many three-digit numbers are divisible by 6 but not by 9?
questions.solution: Multiples of 6 in 100–999: 166 − 16 = 150. Those also divisible by 9 are multiples of 18: 55 − 5 = 50. 150 − 50 = 100.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AB = AC = 13 cm and BC = 10 cm. What is the inradius?
questions.solution: The height to BC is √(13² − 5²) = 12, so area = 60. s = (13 + 13 + 10)/2 = 18. r = Area/s = 60/18 = 10/3 cm.

questions.question: A chord of a circle of radius 10 cm is 6 cm from the centre. What is the length of the chord (in cm)?
questions.solution: Half-chord = √(10² − 6²) = 8, so the chord is 16 cm.

questions.question: From a point P 13 cm from the centre O of a circle of radius 5 cm, tangents PA and PB are drawn. What is the area of quadrilateral OAPB?
questions.solution: Tangent length = √(13² − 5²) = 12. OAPB is two right triangles, each (1/2) × 5 × 12 = 30, so the area is 60 cm².

questions.question: What is the area of a regular hexagon with side 6 cm?
questions.solution: A regular hexagon is 6 equilateral triangles: 6 × (√3/4) × 36 = 54√3 cm².

questions.question: A triangle has vertices (0, 0), (6, 0) and (0, 8). What is the distance between its circumcentre and its incentre?
questions.solution: It's right-angled at the origin, so the circumcentre is the hypotenuse midpoint (3, 4) and R = 5. Inradius r = (6 + 8 − 10)/2 = 2, so the incentre is (2, 2). Distance = √(1² + 2²) = √5. (Check: Euler's OI² = R² − 2Rr = 25 − 20 = 5.)

questions.question: A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into solid cones of base radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. How many cones are made?
questions.solution: Sphere volume = (4/3)π × 216 = 288π. Cone volume = (1/3)π × 9 × 4 = 12π. 288π/12π = 24 cones.

questions.question: A 12 × 8 × 6 cm cuboid is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many cubes have no painted face?
questions.solution: The unpainted cubes form the inner block (12 − 2) × (8 − 2) × (6 − 2) = 10 × 6 × 4 = 240.

questions.question: The space diagonal of a cube is 6√3 cm. What is its total surface area?
questions.solution: Diagonal = a√3 ⇒ a = 6. TSA = 6a² = 216 cm².

questions.question: In how many arrangements of the letters of BANANA are the two N's not next to each other?
questions.solution: Total = 6!/(3! 2!) = 60. With the N's together (treat NN as one block): 5!/3! = 20. Not together = 60 − 20 = 40.

questions.question: In how many ways can 10 identical chocolates be distributed among 4 children so that each child gets at least one?
questions.solution: Give each child one first, then share the remaining 6 freely: C(6 + 3, 3) = C(9, 3) = 84. (Equivalently, C(9, 3) by stars and bars.)

questions.question: How many rectangles (including squares) are there on an 8 × 8 chessboard?
questions.solution: Pick 2 of the 9 horizontal lines and 2 of the 9 vertical lines: C(9, 2)² = 36² = 1,296. (204 is the number of squares.)

questions.question: How many four-digit numbers have digits that strictly increase from left to right (e.g. 1357)?
questions.solution: 0 can't appear (it would have to come first). Any 4 distinct digits from 1–9 can be arranged in increasing order in exactly one way: C(9, 4) = 126.

questions.question: Three fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 10?
Two cards are drawn at random from a standard 52-card deck. What is the probability that both are aces or both are kings?
A and B take turns tossing a fair coin, A first. The first to get a head wins. What is the probability that A wins?
What is the sum of all two-digit numbers that leave remainder 2 when divided by 5?
questions.solution: The numbers are 12, 17, …, 97: an AP with 18 terms. Sum = 18 × (12 + 97)/2 = 981.

questions.question: The 5th term of an AP is 17 and the 12th term is 38. What is the 20th term?
An infinite GP has first term 4 and sum 12. What is the sum of its first three terms?
What is the sum of the first 20 terms of the series 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …?
questions.solution: The terms are triangular numbers k(k + 1)/2. Their sum up to n is n(n + 1)(n + 2)/6 = 20 × 21 × 22/6 = 1,540.

questions.question: The price of a gadget is first raised by 25% and then reduced by x%, so that the final price is 10% above the original price. What is x?
A shopkeeper allows successive discounts of 20% and 10% on the marked price and still earns a profit of 8% on cost price. By what percentage is the marked price above the cost price?
questions.solution: Selling price = 0.8 × 0.9 × MP = 0.72 MP = 1.08 CP. So MP = 1.5 CP, i.e. 50% above cost.

questions.question: A cyclist covers the first half of a journey at 20 km/h. At what speed (in km/h) must he cover the second half so that his average speed for the whole journey is 24 km/h?
questions.solution: Average speed is the harmonic mean for equal distances: 2/(1/20 + 1/v) = 24, so 1/20 + 1/v = 1/12 and 1/v = 1/30. Hence v = 30.

questions.question: A can finish a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves. In how many days in all is the job completed?
questions.solution: In 4 days together: 4 × (1/12 + 1/18) = 4 × 5/36 = 5/9 of the work. The remaining 4/9 is done by B at 1/18 per day, which takes 8 days. Total = 4 + 8 = 12 days.

questions.question: A vessel holds 120 litres of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 2. How many litres of the mixture must be drawn out and replaced by water so that milk and water become equal in quantity?
questions.solution: Milk = 72 L. Removing x litres of mixture removes 0.6x litres of milk. We need 72 − 0.6x = 60, so x = 20.

questions.question: The average of 11 numbers is 30. The average of the first six is 28 and the average of the last six is 33. What is the sixth number?
questions.solution: Sum of all = 330. The sixth number is counted in both groups: 6×28 + 6×33 = 168 + 198 = 366. So the sixth number = 366 − 330 = 36.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2<sup>100</sup> is divided by 7?
How many zeroes does 75! end with?
questions.solution: Count the factors of 5: ⌊75/5⌋ + ⌊75/25⌋ = 15 + 3 = 18.

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 5, find the value of x³ + 1/x³.
The roots of x² − 7x + k = 0 differ by 3. What is the value of k?
questions.solution: Let the roots be a and a + 3. Sum = 2a + 3 = 7, so a = 2. The roots are 2 and 5, so k = product = 10.

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm. What is the radius of its incircle?
A chord of length 24 cm is at a distance of 5 cm from the centre of a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.solution: Half-chord = 12. Radius² = 12² + 5² = 169, so r = 13 cm.

questions.question: Each edge of a cube is increased by 20%. By what percentage (to one decimal place) does its volume increase?
questions.solution: New volume = 1.2³ = 1.728 times the old one, so the increase is 72.8%.

questions.question: A sum of ₹10,000 is invested for 3 years at 10% per annum. Find (in ₹) the difference between the compound interest (annual compounding) and the simple interest.
In how many ways can the letters of the word BANANA be arranged so that no two A's are adjacent?
questions.solution: Arrange B, N, N first: 3!/2! = 3 ways. This creates 4 gaps; choose 3 of them for the A's: C(4,3) = 4. Total = 3 × 4 = 12.

questions.question: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is a prime number?
questions.solution: Prime sums: 2 (1 way), 3 (2), 5 (4), 7 (6), 11 (2) = 15 favourable outcomes out of 36. Probability = 15/36 = 5/12.

questions.question: The sum of the first n terms of a sequence is 3n² + 2n. Find its 10th term.
Three numbers in geometric progression have a sum of 21 and a product of 216. What is the largest of them?
questions.solution: Let them be 6/r, 6, 6r (the middle term is the cube root of 216). Then 6/r + 6 + 6r = 21, so r + 1/r = 5/2, giving r = 2 or 1/2. The numbers are 3, 6, 12, so the largest is 12.

questions.question: If log₂ x + log₄ x = 6, what is x?
questions.solution: log₄ x = (1/2) log₂ x, so (3/2) log₂ x = 6, giving log₂ x = 4 and x = 16.

questions.question: How many integers x satisfy both |x − 3| < 5 and x² ≤ 16?
questions.solution: |x − 3| < 5 gives −2 < x < 8. x² ≤ 16 gives −4 ≤ x ≤ 4. Common integers: −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, which is 6.

questions.question: Two varieties of rice costing ₹40/kg and ₹55/kg are mixed and the mixture is sold at ₹54/kg at a profit of 20%. In what ratio were the cheaper and dearer varieties mixed?
questions.solution: Cost price of the mixture = 54/1.2 = ₹45. By alligation, cheaper : dearer = (55 − 45) : (45 − 40) = 10 : 5 = 2 : 1.

questions.question: A boat travels 36 km downstream in 3 hours and returns the same 36 km upstream in 4.5 hours. What is the speed of the stream in km/h?
questions.solution: Downstream = 12 km/h, upstream = 8 km/h. Stream = (12 − 8)/2 = 2 km/h.

questions.question: Pipe A fills a tank in 20 minutes, pipe B in 30 minutes, and pipe C empties it in 60 minutes. If all three are opened together, in how many minutes is the empty tank filled?
A father is three times as old as his son. Twelve years ago he was seven times as old as the son was then. What is the father's present age (in years)?
questions.solution: F = 3S and F − 12 = 7(S − 12). So 3S − 12 = 7S − 84, giving S = 18 and F = 54.

questions.question: In a class of 60 students, 35 play cricket, 30 play football and 10 play neither. How many students play both games?
questions.solution: Students playing at least one game = 60 − 10 = 50. Both = 35 + 30 − 50 = 15.

questions.question: The price of sugar rises by 25%. By what percentage must a family cut its sugar consumption so that its spending on sugar stays the same?
questions.solution: New price = 1.25 × old. To keep spending equal, consumption must become 1/1.25 = 0.8 of the old, a cut of 20%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells two phones for ₹1,200 each, making a 20% profit on one and a 20% loss on the other. What is his overall result?
questions.solution: Cost prices are 1200/1.2 = ₹1,000 and 1200/0.8 = ₹1,500. Total cost ₹2,500, total revenue ₹2,400, so a loss of ₹100.

questions.question: A 40-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How many litres of water must be added to make the ratio 3 : 2?
questions.solution: Milk = 30 L and water = 10 L. Milk stays 30 L, so for 3 : 2 water must be 20 L. Add 20 − 10 = 10 litres.

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become four times itself at the same rate?
questions.solution: Doubling means the interest equals the principal in 5 years, so the rate is 20% a year. Four times needs interest of 300%, which takes 300/20 = 15 years (not 10: simple interest does not compound).

questions.question: Walking at 5 km/h, Meena reaches her office 6 minutes late. Walking at 6 km/h, she reaches 4 minutes early. How far is her office?
questions.solution: The two times differ by 6 + 4 = 10 minutes = 1/6 h. So d/5 − d/6 = d/30 = 1/6, giving d = 5 km.

questions.question: Two trains, 150 m and 100 m long, run on parallel tracks in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.solution: Relative speed = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Distance to cover = 150 + 100 = 250 m. Time = 250/25 = 10 s.

questions.question: 6 men or 9 women can finish a job in 12 days. In how many days will 4 men and 6 women together finish it?
questions.solution: 6 men = 9 women, so 1 man = 1.5 women. The job is 9 × 12 = 108 woman-days. 4 men + 6 women = 6 + 6 = 12 women, so 108/12 = 9 days.

questions.question: The average age of 30 students in a class is 15 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average rises by 1 year. What is the teacher's age in years?
questions.solution: Students' total = 450. With the teacher, 31 people average 16, total 496. Teacher = 496 − 450 = 46 (the trap is 16: the teacher must also lift everyone else's average by 1).

questions.question: ₹2,100 is divided among A, B and C such that A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5. What is C's share?
Ravi spends 75% of his income. His income rises by 20% and his spending rises by 10%. By what percentage do his savings increase?
questions.solution: Take income 100: spending 75, savings 25. New income 120, new spending 82.5, new savings 37.5. Increase = 12.5/25 = 50%.

questions.question: If α and β are the roots of x² − 5x + 3 = 0, find the value of α² + β².
questions.solution: α + β = 5 and αβ = 3, so α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = 25 − 6 = 19. No need to find the roots.

questions.question: How many integers x satisfy |x − 3| + |x + 2| ≤ 9?
questions.solution: Between −2 and 3 the sum is always 5. For x > 3 it is 2x − 1 ≤ 9, so x ≤ 5; for x < −2 it is 1 − 2x ≤ 9, so x ≥ −4. So x runs from −4 to 5: 10 integers.

questions.question: A function satisfies f(x) + 2f(1/x) = 3x for every x ≠ 0. What is f(2)?
Given log₁₀2 = 0.301, how many digits does 2<sup>50</sup> have?
questions.solution: log₁₀(2<sup>50</sup>) = 50 × 0.301 = 15.05. A number whose log lies between 15 and 16 has 15 + 1 = 16 digits.

questions.question: In an arithmetic progression the 4th term is 14 and the 9th term is 34. What is the sum of its first 20 terms?
questions.solution: 5d = 34 − 14 = 20, so d = 4 and the first term is 14 − 12 = 2. The 20th term is 2 + 76 = 78, so S₂₀ = 20 × (2 + 78)/2 = 800.

questions.question: In a geometric progression with real terms, the 3rd term is 12 and the 6th term is 96. What is the sum of the first 5 terms?
questions.solution: r³ = 96/12 = 8, so r = 2 and the first term is 12/4 = 3. Sum = 3(2⁵ − 1)/(2 − 1) = 93.

questions.question: How many ordered pairs of positive integers (x, y) satisfy 3x + 5y = 100?
questions.solution: 100 − 5y must be a positive multiple of 3. 5y ≡ 1 (mod 3) means y ≡ 2 (mod 3): y = 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 (y = 20 gives x = 0). That is 6 pairs.

questions.question: A right triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the length of the altitude drawn to the hypotenuse?
questions.solution: Hypotenuse = 10. Twice the area = 6 × 8 = 10 × h, so h = 4.8 cm.

questions.question: Two circles of radii 7 cm and 1 cm have their centres 10 cm apart. What is the length of a direct (outer) common tangent?
questions.solution: Direct common tangent = √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²) = √(100 − 36) = 8 cm. (The trap is 6 cm, which uses r₁ + r₂: that is the transverse common tangent, √(100 − 64) = 6.)

questions.question: A solid cube of side 6 cm is cut into identical cubes of side 2 cm. What is the total surface area, in cm², of all the small cubes together?
questions.solution: There are (6/2)³ = 27 small cubes, each with surface area 6 × 2² = 24 cm². Total = 27 × 24 = 648 cm² (three times the original 216 cm²).

questions.question: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 150°. How many diagonals does it have?
questions.solution: Each exterior angle is 30°, so there are 360/30 = 12 sides. Diagonals = 12 × 9/2 = 54.

questions.question: What are the last two digits of 7<sup>42</sup>?
questions.solution: 7⁴ = 2401 ends in 01, so 7⁴⁰ = (7⁴)¹⁰ also ends in 01. Then 7⁴² ends like 01 × 49 = 49.

questions.question: How many divisors of 720 are perfect squares?
questions.solution: 720 = 2⁴ × 3² × 5. A square divisor uses even exponents: 2 in {0, 2, 4} (3 ways), 3 in {0, 2} (2 ways), 5 in {0} (1 way). 3 × 2 × 1 = 6.

questions.question: A committee of 4 is to be chosen from 5 men and 4 women so that it has at least 2 women. In how many ways can this be done?
questions.solution: 2 women: C(4,2) × C(5,2) = 60. 3 women: C(4,3) × 5 = 20. 4 women: 1. Total = 81. (126 is all committees, with no condition.)

questions.question: A number is picked at random from 1 to 50. What is the probability that it is divisible by 3 or by 5?
questions.solution: Multiples of 3: 16, of 5: 10, of both (15): 3. By inclusion–exclusion, 16 + 10 − 3 = 23, so 23/50.

questions.question: A trader claims to sell rice at 10% above cost price, but his weighing scale shows 1 kg when only 800 g is on it. What is his actual profit percentage?
questions.solution: Take the cost of 1 kg as ₹100. The customer pays ₹110 but receives 800 g, which cost the trader ₹80. Profit = 30/80 = 37.5%.

questions.question: In a 1 km race, A beats B by 100 m, and B beats C by 100 m. By how many metres does A beat C in a 1 km race?
questions.solution: When A runs 1000 m, B runs 900 m. When B runs 1000 m, C runs 900 m, so when B runs 900 m, C runs 810 m. A beats C by 1000 − 810 = 190 m. (Adding 100 + 100 is the trap.)

questions.question: Two trains start at the same time from stations P and Q and travel towards each other. After they meet, the train from P takes 9 hours to reach Q and the train from Q takes 16 hours to reach P. The faster train runs at 80 km/h. What is the distance PQ in km?
questions.solution: If they meet after t hours with speeds a (from P) and b (from Q): a·t = 16b and b·t = 9a. Dividing, (a/b)² = 16/9, so a : b = 4 : 3. The faster train (from P) is 80 km/h, so b = 60 km/h. Then t = 16 × 60 / 80 = 12 hours, and PQ = (80 + 60) × 12 = 1680 km.

questions.question: A and B together can finish a job in 12 days. A works alone for 6 days, and then B alone finishes the remaining work in 16 days. In how many days can A alone finish the whole job?
questions.solution: Let A's daily rate be a. Then B's rate is 1/12 − a, and 6a + 16(1/12 − a) = 1. So 4/3 − 10a = 1, giving a = 1/30. A alone needs 30 days.

questions.question: A sum of money at compound interest (compounded annually) amounts to ₹8,820 in 2 years and ₹9,261 in 3 years. What is the sum?
questions.solution: One year's growth: 9261 / 8820 = 1.05, so the rate is 5%. Principal = 8820 / 1.05² = 8820 / 1.1025 = ₹8,000.

questions.question: Find the smallest integer k for which both roots of x² − (k + 1)x + (k + 4) = 0 are real and positive.
questions.solution: Real roots: (k + 1)² − 4(k + 4) ≥ 0, i.e. k² − 2k − 15 ≥ 0, i.e. (k − 5)(k + 3) ≥ 0, so k ≥ 5 or k ≤ −3. Positive roots need sum k + 1 > 0 and product k + 4 > 0, i.e. k > −1. Together: k ≥ 5, so the smallest is 5 (roots 3 and 3).

questions.question: How many integers x satisfy |x − 2| + |x + 3| ≤ 9?
questions.solution: For −3 ≤ x ≤ 2 the sum is always 5, which is fine. For x > 2: 2x + 1 ≤ 9, so x ≤ 4. For x < −3: −2x − 1 ≤ 9, so x ≥ −5. So x runs from −5 to 4: 10 integers.

questions.question: What is the minimum value of |x − 1| + |x − 4| + |x − 9| over all real x?
questions.solution: A sum of distances from points is smallest at the median point, x = 4: 3 + 0 + 5 = 8.

questions.question: If log<sub>a</sub> b = 2 and log<sub>b</sub> c = 3, what is log<sub>ac</sub> b?
questions.solution: b = a² and c = b³ = a⁶, so ac = a⁷. Then log<sub>ac</sub> b = log(a²)/log(a⁷) = 2/7.

questions.question: x and y are positive real numbers with x + y = 10. What is the maximum value of x²y?
questions.solution: Write 10 = x/2 + x/2 + y. By AM ≥ GM, (x/2)(x/2)(y) ≤ (10/3)³, so x²y ≤ 4 × 1000/27 = 4000/27, reached at x = 20/3, y = 10/3. (2000/9 is larger, but it cannot be reached.)

questions.question: The sum of an infinite geometric progression is 20, and the sum of the squares of its terms is 100. What is its first term?
questions.solution: a/(1 − r) = 20 and a²/(1 − r²) = 100. Dividing the second by the square of the first: (1 − r)/(1 + r) = 100/400 = 1/4, so r = 3/5. Then a = 20 × (2/5) = 8.

questions.question: How many divisors of 7200 are perfect squares?
questions.solution: 7200 = 2⁵ × 3² × 5². A square divisor needs even powers: 2 can have power 0, 2 or 4 (3 ways), 3 can have 0 or 2 (2 ways), 5 can have 0 or 2 (2 ways). Total = 3 × 2 × 2 = 12.

questions.question: What are the last two digits of 3<sup>2026</sup>?
The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 720. How many such pairs of numbers exist? (Treat (a, b) and (b, a) as the same pair.)
questions.solution: Write the numbers as 12m and 12n with m, n co-prime and mn = 720/12 = 60 = 2² × 3 × 5. Each of the three prime powers goes wholly to m or to n: 2³ = 8 ordered ways, so 4 unordered pairs: (12, 720), (36, 240), (48, 180), (60, 144).

questions.question: How many ordered pairs of positive integers (x, y) satisfy 1/x + 1/y = 1/6?
questions.solution: Clearing fractions: xy − 6x − 6y = 0, i.e. (x − 6)(y − 6) = 36. Both factors must be positive (if both were negative, each would be at least −5 and their product at most 25). 36 has 9 divisors, so there are 9 ordered pairs.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AB = 10 cm and AC = 14 cm. The bisector of angle A meets BC at D, and BD = 5 cm. What is the length of AD?
questions.solution: Angle bisector theorem: BD/DC = AB/AC = 10/14, so DC = 7. Bisector length: AD² = AB × AC − BD × DC = 140 − 35 = 105, so AD = √105 cm.

questions.question: Two circles of radii 9 cm and 4 cm touch each other externally. What is the length (in cm) of their direct common tangent?
questions.solution: The distance between centres is 9 + 4 = 13. Direct common tangent = √(13² − (9 − 4)²) = √(169 − 25) = 12 cm.

questions.question: What is the area (in square units) of the region defined by |x| + |2y| ≤ 6?
questions.solution: The boundary is a rhombus with vertices (±6, 0) and (0, ±3). Its diagonals are 12 and 6, so area = (12 × 6)/2 = 36.

questions.question: A right circular cone of height 30 cm is cut by a plane parallel to its base, at a height of 10 cm above the base. What is the ratio of the volume of the small cone (on top) to the volume of the frustum?
questions.solution: The small cone has height 20, so it is similar to the full cone with ratio 2/3. Volumes scale as the cube: small = 8/27 of the whole, so the frustum = 19/27. Ratio = 8 : 19. (8 : 27 compares with the whole cone, not the frustum.)

questions.question: In how many ways can 10 identical chocolates be distributed among 3 children so that each child gets at least 1 and at most 5?
questions.solution: Give each child 1 first: now a + b + c = 7 with each between 0 and 4. Without the upper limit: C(9, 2) = 36. Subtract the cases where one child gets 5 or more: set that child's share to 5 + a', leaving 2 to share: C(4, 2) = 6 ways, for each of 3 children = 18. Two children cannot both exceed. Answer = 36 − 18 = 18.

questions.question: A bag has 5 red and 4 blue balls. Three balls are drawn together at random. What is the probability that the three balls include both colours?
questions.solution: Total ways = C(9, 3) = 84. All red: C(5, 3) = 10; all blue: C(4, 3) = 4. Probability = 1 − 14/84 = 70/84 = 5/6.

questions.question: In a survey of 100 people, 80 like tea, 75 like coffee and 70 like juice. What is the minimum number of people who like all three?
questions.solution: People who do not like tea, coffee and juice number 20, 25 and 30. Even if these groups do not overlap, at most 75 people miss at least one drink. So at least 100 − 75 = 25 like all three.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 20% of the registered voters did not vote, and 5% of the votes cast were invalid. The winner got 55% of the valid votes and won by 1,520 votes. How many voters were registered?
questions.solution: Let N be the number of registered voters. Valid votes = 0.8 × 0.95 × N = 0.76N. The margin is 55% − 45% = 10% of the valid votes: 0.076N = 1520, so N = 20,000.

questions.question: A shop runs a "buy 3, get 1 free" offer and still makes a profit of 20%. By what percentage is the marked price above the cost price?
questions.solution: Take the cost of one item as 100. The customer pays for 3 and takes 4, so 3 × MP = 1.2 × 400 = 480, giving MP = 160. The marked price is 60% above cost.

questions.question: A man rows to a place 24 km away and comes back, taking 10 hours in all. He finds that he can row 4 km downstream in the same time as 2 km upstream. What is the speed of the stream in km/h?
questions.solution: Downstream speed is twice the upstream speed: d = 2u. Then 24/(2u) + 24/u = 36/u = 10, so u = 3.6 and d = 7.2 km/h. Stream = (7.2 − 3.6)/2 = 1.8 km/h.

questions.question: A and B start together from the same point on a circular track of length 600 m and run in opposite directions at 15 m/s and 25 m/s. If they keep running, at how many distinct points on the track will they meet?
questions.solution: Their speeds are in the ratio 3 : 5. Running in opposite directions, they meet at (3 + 5) = 8 distinct points. Check: relative speed 40 m/s, so they meet every 15 s; A covers 225 m between meetings, and 225 × 8 = 1800 = 3 laps, so the pattern repeats after 8 meetings.

questions.question: A and B start a business with ₹40,000 and ₹60,000. After 4 months, A adds ₹20,000 and B withdraws ₹10,000. The profit at the end of the year is ₹55,000. What is A's share?
questions.solution: A: 40,000 × 4 + 60,000 × 8 = 6,40,000 rupee-months. B: 60,000 × 4 + 50,000 × 8 = 6,40,000. The shares are equal, so A gets ₹27,500. (Using only the starting amounts gives ₹22,000, the trap.)

questions.question: A loan of ₹21,000 at 10% per annum compound interest is repaid in two equal annual instalments, the first one year after the loan. What is each instalment (in ₹)?
questions.solution: The present values of the two instalments add up to the loan: x/1.1 + x/1.21 = 21000. Multiply by 1.21: 1.1x + x = 25410, so x = ₹12,100.

questions.question: How many times in a day (24 hours) are the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at right angles?
questions.solution: The minute hand gains 330° on the hour hand every hour, so in 12 hours it gains 11 full rounds and passes each right-angle position (90° and 270°) 11 times: 22 times in 12 hours, 44 in a day. (48 assumes two right angles in every hour, but the ones at exactly 3:00 and 9:00 each serve two neighbouring hours, so 2 are lost in every 12 hours.)

questions.question: If α and β are the roots of x² − 4x + 1 = 0, what is the value of α⁴ + β⁴?
How many integers x with −10 ≤ x ≤ 10 satisfy (x − 1)(x − 5)/(x − 3) ≤ 0?
questions.solution: Mark the critical points 1, 3, 5. The expression is ≤ 0 for x ≤ 1 and for 3 < x ≤ 5 (x = 3 is not allowed). In range: −10 to 1 gives 12 integers, and 4, 5 give 2 more. Total = 14.

questions.question: If f(x) = (x − 1)/(x + 1), what is f(f(f(f(f(3)))))?
questions.solution: f(3) = 1/2, f(1/2) = −1/3, f(−1/3) = −2, f(−2) = 3. The values repeat every 4 steps, so the fifth application gives f(3) = 1/2.

questions.question: If 2<sup>x</sup> = 3<sup>y</sup> = 6<sup>z</sup> (with x, y, z non-zero), which of these is true?
questions.solution: Let the common value be k. Then x = log k / log 2, y = log k / log 3, z = log k / log 6. So 1/x + 1/y = (log 2 + log 3)/log k = log 6/log k = 1/z, which gives z = xy/(x + y).

questions.question: When a polynomial p(x) is divided by (x − 1) the remainder is 3, and when divided by (x − 2) the remainder is 5. What is the remainder when p(x) is divided by (x − 1)(x − 2)?
questions.solution: The remainder has the form ax + b. From the remainder theorem: a + b = 3 and 2a + b = 5, so a = 2, b = 1. Remainder = 2x + 1.

questions.question: In an arithmetic progression, the 4th term is three times the 1st term, and the 7th term is 1 more than twice the 3rd term. What is the sum of the first 10 terms?
Real numbers x and y satisfy x² + y² = 25. What is the maximum value of 3x + 4y?
questions.solution: By the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, (3x + 4y)² ≤ (3² + 4²)(x² + y²) = 25 × 25, so 3x + 4y ≤ 25, reached at x = 3, y = 4. (35 would need x = y = 5, which is not on the circle.)

questions.question: What is the highest power of 12 that divides 50! exactly?
questions.solution: 12 = 2² × 3. Powers of 2 in 50!: 25 + 12 + 6 + 3 + 1 = 47, which gives 23 factors of 4. Powers of 3: 16 + 5 + 1 = 22. The smaller count decides: 22.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 7<sup>99</sup> is divided by 2400?
How many integers from 1 to 1000 are divisible by none of 2, 3 and 5?
questions.solution: Inclusion–exclusion. Divisible by 2, 3, 5: 500, 333, 200. By 6, 10, 15: 166, 100, 66. By 30: 33. Divisible by at least one = 1033 − 332 + 33 = 734. None = 1000 − 734 = 266.

questions.question: What is the sum of all the odd divisors of 360?
questions.solution: 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5. Odd divisors come from 3² × 5 = 45. Their sum = (1 + 3 + 9)(1 + 5) = 13 × 6 = 78.

questions.question: In trapezium ABCD, AB is parallel to CD and AB = 2 × CD. The diagonals meet at O. If the area of triangle COD is 12 sq cm, what is the area of the trapezium (in sq cm)?
questions.solution: Triangles AOB and COD are similar with ratio 2 : 1, so area AOB = 4 × 12 = 48. Since AO : OC = 2 : 1, triangle AOD = 2 × COD = 24, and likewise BOC = 24. Total = 12 + 48 + 24 + 24 = 108.

questions.question: An equilateral triangle is inscribed in a circle of radius 6 cm. What is the area of the part of the circle that lies outside the triangle?
questions.solution: Side of the triangle = R√3 = 6√3. Area of triangle = (√3/4)(6√3)² = 27√3. Circle = 36π. Required area = 36π − 27√3 sq cm.

questions.question: The line 3x + 4y = 24 forms a triangle with the coordinate axes. What is the distance of the incentre of this triangle from the origin?
questions.solution: The triangle has legs 8 and 6 and hypotenuse 10. For a right triangle, inradius = (6 + 8 − 10)/2 = 2, and the incentre is (2, 2). Distance from origin = 2√2.

questions.question: A committee of 5 is to be formed from 6 men and 5 women. It must have at least 2 women, and a particular man M and a particular woman W refuse to serve together. In how many ways can the committee be formed?
questions.solution: With at least 2 women: C(5,2)C(6,3) + C(5,3)C(6,2) + C(5,4)C(6,1) + C(5,5) = 200 + 150 + 30 + 1 = 381. Committees with both M and W: choose 3 more from 5 men and 4 women with at least 1 more woman: C(9,3) − C(5,3) = 84 − 10 = 74. Answer = 381 − 74 = 307.

questions.question: In how many ways can 5 boys and 5 girls sit around a round table so that no two boys sit next to each other?
questions.solution: Seat the girls first around the table: (5 − 1)! = 24 ways. This leaves 5 gaps, one between each pair of girls, for the 5 boys: 5! = 120 ways. Total = 24 × 120 = 2880.

questions.question: A family has two children. You are told that at least one of them is a boy. What is the probability that both are boys? (Assume each child is equally likely to be a boy or a girl.)
questions.solution: The equally likely cases are BB, BG, GB, GG. "At least one boy" leaves BB, BG, GB. Only BB has two boys, so the probability is 1/3. (1/2 is the common trap.)

questions.question: Two different numbers are chosen at random from 1 to 20. What is the probability that their sum is even?
questions.solution: The sum is even when both are even or both are odd: C(10,2) + C(10,2) = 45 + 45 = 90. Total = C(20,2) = 190. Probability = 90/190 = 9/19. (It is not 1/2 because the two numbers must be different.)

questions.question: Two cyclists start at the same moment from towns P and Q, 252 km apart, riding towards each other at constant speeds. After they cross, the first takes 4 hours to reach Q and the second takes 9 hours to reach P. What is the speed of the first cyclist, in km/h?
questions.solution: If they meet after t hours, t² = 4 × 9, so t = 6. The speed ratio is √(9/4) = 3 : 2, and the combined speed is 252/6 = 42 km/h. The first cyclist's speed is 42 × 3/5 = 25.2 km/h.

questions.question: A and B together can finish a job in 12 days. They work together for 4 days, after which A leaves and B finishes the rest in 20 more days. Had C, who is twice as efficient as B, joined A and B from the start, how many days would the whole job have taken?
questions.solution: A + B do 1/12 per day, so in 4 days they finish 1/3. B does the remaining 2/3 in 20 days, so B alone takes 30 days and C does 1/15 per day. Then A + B + C do 1/12 + 1/15 = 9/60 = 3/20 per day, and the job takes 20/3 days ≈ 6.67 days.

questions.question: A vessel holds 80 litres of pure milk. Some milk is drawn off and replaced with water, and the same volume of the mixture is then drawn off again and replaced with water. The vessel now contains 45 litres of milk. How many litres were drawn off each time?
A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price. What discount percentage must he offer on the marked price so that his profit is 12%?
questions.solution: With CP = 100, MP = 140 and the required SP is 112. The discount is 28 on 140, which is 20%.

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 10% per annum is ₹930. What is the sum, in ₹?
The monthly salaries of Asha and Bilal are in the ratio 5 : 7. If each gets a raise of ₹4,000, the ratio becomes 3 : 4. What is Asha's original salary, in ₹?
questions.solution: Let the salaries be 5k and 7k. Then 4(5k + 4000) = 3(7k + 4000), so 20k + 16000 = 21k + 12000 and k = 4000. Asha earns 5k = ₹20,000.

questions.question: The average of a list of numbers is 36. When one number, 60, is removed, the average of the remaining numbers becomes 34.5. How many numbers were in the original list?
A boat makes a round trip of 84 km upstream and 84 km back downstream in 10 hours. The upstream leg takes 4 hours more than the downstream leg. What is the speed of the boat in still water, in km/h?
questions.solution: Downstream takes 3 h and upstream 7 h. So b + s = 28 and b − s = 12, giving b = 20 km/h.

questions.question: For how many integer values of k does the equation x² − kx + k + 8 = 0 have two distinct integer roots?
questions.solution: If the roots are r and s, then r + s = k and rs = k + 8, so rs − r − s = 8, i.e. (r − 1)(s − 1) = 9. Factor pairs of 9 with r ≠ s: (1, 9), (9, 1), (−1, −9), (−9, −1) give root pairs {2, 10} and {0, −8}, so k = 12 or −8. The pair (3, 3) or (−3, −3) gives equal roots and is excluded. Answer: 2.

questions.question: How many integers x with |x| ≤ 20 satisfy (x² − 5x − 14)(x − 3) < 0?
questions.solution: (x² − 5x − 14)(x − 3) = (x + 2)(x − 3)(x − 7). The product is negative for x < −2 or 3 < x < 7. With |x| ≤ 20 this gives x = −20, …, −3 (18 integers) and x = 4, 5, 6 (3 integers), 21 in all.

questions.question: If log₂x + log₄x + log₁₆x = 7, what is the value of x?
questions.solution: Writing everything in base 2: log₂x (1 + 1/2 + 1/4) = 7, so (7/4) log₂x = 7, giving log₂x = 4 and x = 16.

questions.question: A function f satisfies f(x) + 2f(1 − x) = x² for every real x. What is f(3)?
questions.solution: Put x = 3: f(3) + 2f(−2) = 9. Put x = −2: f(−2) + 2f(3) = 4. Doubling the second and subtracting the first: 3f(3) = 8 − 9 = −1, so f(3) = −1/3.

questions.question: The sum of the first 10 terms of an arithmetic progression is 155 and the sum of the first 20 terms is 610. What is the sum of the 21st to the 30th terms?
How many ordered pairs of integers (x, y) satisfy |x| + 2|y| ≤ 6?
questions.solution: For each y with |y| ≤ 3, x ranges over |x| ≤ 6 − 2|y|, giving 2(6 − 2|y|) + 1 values: y = 0 gives 13; |y| = 1 gives 9 (twice); |y| = 2 gives 5 (twice); |y| = 3 gives 1 (twice). Total 13 + 18 + 10 + 2 = 43.

questions.question: x and y are non-negative real numbers with x + y = 10. What is the maximum possible value of x²y? (Give the answer as a fraction or decimal if needed.)
A right triangle has legs of length 20 and 21. What is the product of its inradius and circumradius?
questions.solution: The hypotenuse is √(400 + 441) = 29. Inradius = (20 + 21 − 29)/2 = 6, circumradius = 29/2. Product = 87.

questions.question: Two parallel chords of a circle of radius 13 cm lie on the same side of the centre. One chord is 24 cm long and the distance between the chords is 7 cm. What is the length of the other chord, in cm?
questions.solution: The 24 cm chord is √(169 − 144) = 5 cm from the centre. The other is 12 cm from the centre (same side, 7 cm further), so its half-length is √(169 − 144) = 5 and its length 10 cm.

questions.question: What is the area of the quadrilateral with vertices (0, 0), (8, 0), (8, 6) and (2, 9), taken in that order?
How many integers from 1 to 1000 are divisible by exactly one of 3, 5 and 7?
What is the remainder when 7^2026 is divided by 100?
In how many distinct ways can the letters A, A, B, B, C, D be arranged in a row so that no two identical letters are next to each other?
questions.solution: Total arrangements = 6!/(2!2!) = 180. Arrangements with the two A's together: treat AA as one block: 5!/2! = 60; similarly 60 for BB. Both together: 4! = 24. Required = 180 − 60 − 60 + 24 = 84.

questions.question: Three fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is even and at least one die shows a 6?
questions.solution: Even-sum outcomes: 108 of 216. Even-sum outcomes with no 6 use faces 1–5 (three odd, two even): all even = 2³ = 8, exactly two odd = 3 × 3² × 2 = 54, so 62 even-sum outcomes have no 6. Hence 108 − 62 = 46 favourable outcomes; probability 46/216 = 23/108.

questions.question: A trader buys 60 kg of rice. He sells one-third of it at a 20% profit and half of the remainder at a 10% loss. At what profit percentage must he sell the rest to make an overall profit of 12%?
questions.solution: Take CP = 1 per kg (total 60). 20 kg earn 24, 20 kg earn 18, so the last 20 kg must earn 67.2 − 42 = 25.2, a profit of 5.2/20 = 26%.

questions.question: Cars A and B start at the same moment from towns P and Q respectively and drive towards each other. After they meet, A takes 4 more hours to reach Q and B takes 9 more hours to reach P. P and Q are 180 km apart, and on reaching the far town each car immediately turns back and keeps shuttling at its constant speed. How many hours after the start do the two cars meet for the second time?
questions.solution: Step 1: if they meet after t hours, A covers in 4 h what B covered in t h and vice versa, so t² = 4 × 9 and t = 6 h; speeds are in the ratio √(9/4) = 3 : 2. Step 2: 6(vA + vB) = 180 with vA : vB = 3 : 2 gives vA = 18, vB = 12 km/h. Step 3: A reaches Q at 10 h and B reaches P at 15 h; in between both head towards P, A from Q and B ahead of it, and A would catch B only at t = 30, so no overtaking occurs. Step 4: a second head-on meeting needs combined distance 3 × 180 = 540 km, i.e. t = 540/30 = 18 h. Check: A has gone 324 km (36 km from P on the way back), B 216 km (36 km from P on the way back to Q).

questions.question: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours and pipe B in 18 hours, while outlet C empties a full tank in 9 hours. All three are opened together on an empty tank and C is closed after 3 hours. How many hours in all does it take to fill the tank?
questions.solution: Rates: A + B − C = 1/12 + 1/18 − 1/9 = 1/36 per hour, so after 3 h the tank is 1/12 full. The remaining 11/12 at 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per hour takes (11/12)(36/5) = 6.6 h. Total 3 + 6.6 = 9.6 hours.

questions.question: Alloy X contains copper and zinc in the ratio 3 : 5 and alloy Y in the ratio 5 : 3. How many kg of Y must be melted with 24 kg of X to obtain an alloy with copper and zinc in the ratio 7 : 9?
questions.solution: Copper fractions: X 3/8, Y 5/8, target 7/16. By alligation, X : Y = (5/8 − 7/16) : (7/16 − 3/8) = 3/16 : 1/16 = 3 : 1. So Y = 24/3 = 8 kg.

questions.question: A sum doubles in 5 years at a certain rate of compound interest (compounded annually). In how many years will it become 16 times itself at the same rate?
questions.solution: Doubling every 5 years: 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 takes four doublings, 4 × 5 = 20 years.

questions.question: ₹7,800 is divided among P, Q and R so that 2 × (P's share) = 3 × (Q's share) = 4 × (R's share). What is Q's share, in ₹?
Four years ago, the average age of a family of 6 was 22 years. A child has been born since then, and today the average age of the 7 members is 22.5 years. How old is the child, in years?
questions.solution: Four years ago the six totalled 132; today they total 132 + 24 = 156. The seven total 7 × 22.5 = 157.5, so the child is 1.5 years old.

questions.question: If α and β are the roots of x² − 6x + 4 = 0, what is the value of α⁴ + β⁴?
How many integers n satisfy (n − 1)(n − 4)(n − 9)(n − 16) < 0 and 1 ≤ n ≤ 25?
questions.solution: The sign is negative between consecutive roots of alternating sign: 1 < n < 4 (n = 2, 3) and 9 < n < 16 (n = 10, …, 15). That gives 2 + 6 = 8 integers.

questions.question: Real numbers x, y > 1 satisfy (log₂x)(log₄y) = 3 and log_x 2 + log_y 2 = 5/6. What is the value of x + y?
questions.solution: Let a = log₂x and b = log₂y (both positive). Then log₄y = b/2, so ab/2 = 3 and ab = 6. Also 1/a + 1/b = (a + b)/ab = 5/6, so a + b = 5. Hence {a, b} = {2, 3}, so {x, y} = {4, 8} and x + y = 12 in either order.

questions.question: For f(x) = (2x + 3)/(x − 1), x ≠ 1, what is f(f(f(2)))?
The 3rd and 6th terms of a geometric progression are 18 and 486. What is the sum of the first 6 terms?
questions.solution: r³ = 486/18 = 27, so r = 3 and the first term is 18/9 = 2. Sum = 2(3⁶ − 1)/(3 − 1) = 728.

questions.question: Positive integers a, b satisfy 1/a + 1/b = 1/12. How many ordered pairs (a, b) are there?
questions.solution: (a − 12)(b − 12) = 144, and both factors must be positive (negative factors would make a or b ≤ 0). 144 = 2⁴ × 3² has 5 × 3 = 15 divisors, so 15 ordered pairs.

questions.question: For real x, what is the minimum value of |x − 2| + |x − 5| + |x − 11|?
questions.solution: The sum of distances is minimised at the median, x = 5: 3 + 0 + 6 = 9.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AB = 13, BC = 14 and CA = 15. What is the length of the altitude from A to BC?
questions.solution: By Heron: s = 21, area = √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = 84. Altitude from A = 2 × 84/14 = 12.

questions.question: A square is inscribed in a semicircle of radius 5√5, with one side of the square on the diameter. What is the area of the square?
questions.solution: With side s, the top corners are at (±s/2, s), so s²/4 + s² = 125, s² = 100.

questions.question: A solid metal cylinder of radius 6 cm and height 32 cm is melted and recast into spheres of radius 2 cm. How many spheres are obtained?
questions.solution: Cylinder volume = π × 36 × 32 = 1152π. Each sphere = (4/3)π × 8 = (32/3)π. Number = 1152 × 3/32 = 108.

questions.question: How many positive divisors of 10800 are perfect squares?
questions.solution: 10800 = 2⁴ × 3³ × 5². A square divisor uses even exponents: 2: {0, 2, 4} (3), 3: {0, 2} (2), 5: {0, 2} (2). Total 12.

questions.question: What is the largest power of 6 that divides 50! ? (Enter the exponent.)
questions.solution: Power of 3 in 50! = 16 + 5 + 1 = 22; power of 2 = 47. The limiting factor is 3, so the exponent is 22.

questions.question: A committee of 5 is chosen from 6 men and 5 women so that it contains at least 2 women and at least 2 men. In how many ways can this be done?
questions.solution: Either 3 men + 2 women: 20 × 10 = 200, or 2 men + 3 women: 15 × 10 = 150. Total 350.

questions.question: Two numbers are chosen at random, without replacement, from {1, 2, …, 20}. What is the probability that their product is a multiple of 4?
questions.solution: Not a multiple of 4: both odd (C(10,2) = 45) or one odd and one ≡ 2 mod 4 (10 × 5 = 50). So 95 of 190 pairs fail, and the probability is 95/190 = 1/2.

questions.question: On a circular track of 1200 m, A and B start together from the same point in the same direction at 8 m/s and 5 m/s. After how many seconds do they meet for the first time at the starting point?
questions.solution: A takes 150 s per lap and B 240 s, so both are at the start together after LCM(150, 240) = 1200 s.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks every item 40% above cost. Cash buyers get a discount of d% on the marked price and card buyers get 2d%. In a month, the cost value of goods bought by card buyers was twice that bought by cash buyers, and his overall profit on cost was 12%. What is d?
questions.solution: Take cost 1 for cash sales and 2 for card sales (total 3). Revenue = 1.4(1 − d/100) + 2 × 1.4(1 − 2d/100) = 1.4(3 − 5d/100). Setting this equal to 3 × 1.12 = 3.36 gives 3 − 5d/100 = 2.4, so d = 12.

questions.question: P, Q and R can each finish a job alone in 20, 30 and 12 days respectively. They charge ₹1,500, ₹1,200 and ₹2,400 per day; a part-day is paid as a full day. Any of them may be hired on any day, and the job must be finished within 8 days. What is the minimum possible total wage bill, in ₹?
questions.solution: Step 1: cost of a whole job by each worker: P 20 × 1500 = 30,000, Q 30 × 1200 = 36,000, R 12 × 2400 = 28,800, so R is cheapest per unit of work, then P, then Q. Step 2: no one may work more than 8 days, so R does at most 8/12 = 2/3. Step 3: the remaining 1/3 is cheapest with P: 1/3 × 20 = 6.67, i.e. 7 paid days. But paying 7 full days wastes part of a day; compare R 8 + P 7 = 19,200 + 10,500 = 29,700 with R 7 + P 8 (7/12 + 8/20 = 0.983, not enough) and with R 8 + P 6 + Q 1 (2/3 + 0.3 + 1/30 = 1, cost 19,200 + 9,000 + 1,200 = 29,400). Step 4: checking all combinations, the minimum is ₹29,400.

questions.question: 12 men can finish a project in 18 days and 18 women can finish it in 24 days. 8 men and 12 women start the project together; after 6 days, 4 more women join them. How many days in all does the project take?
questions.solution: One man does 1/216 of the work per day and one woman 1/432. 8 men + 12 women do 16/432 + 12/432 = 28/432 per day; in 6 days, 168/432. The remaining 264/432 at (16 + 16)/432 = 32/432 per day takes 8.25 days. Total 14.25 days.

questions.question: Solution A is 30% acid and solution B is 75% acid. In what ratio must A and B be mixed to get a 48% acid solution? Enter the ratio A : B as a single number A/B.
A sum of ₹12,000 is invested at 10% per annum compounded half-yearly. What is the interest earned in the first 1.5 years, in ₹?
The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 7 : 5. After 8 boys leave and 4 girls join, the ratio becomes 1 : 1. How many students were originally in the class?
questions.solution: 7k − 8 = 5k + 4 gives k = 6, so the class had 12k = 72 students.

questions.question: The average of 11 consecutive odd numbers is 47. What is the product of the smallest and the largest of them?
questions.solution: The middle (6th) number is 47; the smallest is 47 − 10 = 37 and the largest 47 + 10 = 57. Product = 2109.

questions.question: For how many integers k with 1 ≤ k ≤ 30 does the equation x² + kx + 36 = 0 have two distinct real roots, both negative?
questions.solution: Both roots negative requires the sum −k < 0 (true for k ≥ 1) and product 36 > 0 (true). Distinct real roots need k² > 144, i.e. k ≥ 13. So k = 13, …, 30: 18 values.

questions.question: How many integers x satisfy |x − 3| + |x + 5| < 14?
questions.solution: For −5 ≤ x ≤ 3 the sum is 8 < 14 (9 integers). For x > 3: 2x + 2 < 14 gives x < 6, i.e. 4, 5. For x < −5: −2x − 2 < 14 gives x > −8, i.e. −7, −6. Total 9 + 2 + 2 = 13.

questions.question: If log 2 = 0.3010 and log 3 = 0.4771, how many digits does 6^20 have?
f is a function on the positive integers with f(1) = 2 and f(n + 1) = f(n) + 2n + 1 for all n ≥ 1. What is f(30)?
How many terms of the arithmetic progression 3, 7, 11, … are needed for the sum to exceed 2000 for the first time?
Real numbers x, y satisfy x + y = 7 and x³ + y³ = 133. What is x² + y²?
questions.solution: x³ + y³ = (x + y)³ − 3xy(x + y): 133 = 343 − 21xy, so xy = 10. Then x² + y² = 49 − 20 = 29.

questions.question: What is the maximum value of 8 − |x − 3| − |2x − 10| over real x?
questions.solution: g(x) = |x − 3| + |2x − 10| is piecewise linear with corners at 3 and 5: g(3) = 4, g(5) = 2. Its minimum is 2 at x = 5, so the maximum of 8 − g is 6.

questions.question: In triangle PQR, the bisector of angle P meets QR at S. PQ = 12, PR = 18 and QR = 20. What is QS?
questions.solution: By the angle bisector theorem, QS/SR = 12/18 = 2/3, so QS = 20 × 2/5 = 8.

questions.question: Two circles have radii 5 cm and 3 cm, and their centres are 17 cm apart. What is the length, in cm, of a transverse (internal) common tangent between the points of contact?
questions.solution: Transverse tangent length = √(d² − (r₁ + r₂)²) = √(289 − 64) = √225 = 15.

questions.question: A regular hexagon has side 6 cm. What is the area, in cm², of the triangle formed by joining three alternate vertices of the hexagon? Enter your answer as a multiple of √3 (e.g. 27 if the area is 27√3).
questions.solution: Alternate vertices form an equilateral triangle of side 6√3, with area (√3/4) × 108 = 27√3.

questions.question: A right circular cone is cut by a plane parallel to its base at one-third of its height from the apex. The volume of the frustum is what multiple of the volume of the small cone?
questions.solution: The small cone has linear ratio 1/3, so its volume is 1/27 of the full cone. The frustum is 26/27, i.e. 26 times the small cone.

questions.question: What is the sum of all positive divisors of 360 that are odd?
questions.solution: 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5. Odd divisors are divisors of 45: their sum is (1 + 3 + 9)(1 + 5) = 78.

questions.question: N is the smallest positive integer that leaves remainders 2, 3 and 4 when divided by 3, 4 and 5 respectively, and is also a multiple of 7. What is N?
questions.solution: Remainders are each one less than the divisor, so N + 1 is a multiple of 60: N = 59, 119, 179, … The first multiple of 7 is 119.

questions.question: How many 4-digit numbers have digits in strictly increasing order from left to right?
questions.solution: Choose any 4 distinct digits from 1–9 (0 cannot appear, as it would have to lead); each choice gives exactly one increasing number: C(9, 4) = 126.

questions.question: A bag has 5 red and 7 blue balls. Three balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that exactly two are red?
A shopkeeper marks an item 40% above cost and then offers two successive discounts of 10% and x%. If he still makes a profit of 13.4%, what is x?

A trader uses a faulty balance. When buying, he receives 1100 g for every 1 kg he pays for; when selling, he gives only 900 g for every 1 kg he charges for. If he sells at his cost price per kg, what is his profit percentage?
questions.solution: For ₹C he receives 1100 g. He sells it as 1100/900 = 11/9 'kg' at ₹C each, so revenue is 11C/9. Profit = 2/9 = 22 2/9 %.

questions.question: The average score of 5 boys and 3 girls in a test is 30. All boys scored the same, all girls scored the same, and each girl's score is at least the boys' score but at most 1.5 times it. Scores need not be integers. How many distinct integer values can the total score of 3 boys and 5 girls take?
questions.solution: Step 1: 5b + 3g = 240, so g = (240 − 5b)/3. Step 2: g ≥ b gives b ≤ 30; g ≤ 1.5b gives 240 − 5b ≤ 4.5b, so b ≥ 240/9.5 ≈ 25.26. Step 3: the required total is 3b + 5g = 400 − (16/3)b, which decreases continuously from about 265.26 (at b ≈ 25.26) to 240 (at b = 30). Step 4: integers 240, 241, …, 265, which is 26 values.

questions.question: A can do a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. They work on alternate days, A starting. On which day is the job completed?
questions.solution: In 2 days they do 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12. After 22 days, 11/12 is done. On day 23 A does 1/20, making 11/12 + 1/20 = 58/60, still short. On day 24 B does 1/30, making 60/60. So the job is completed on day 24.

questions.question: A vessel holds 80 litres of pure milk. 8 litres are removed and replaced with water, and this is done three times in all. A further 20 litres of the mixture is then removed and replaced with water. What is the quantity of milk, in litres, now in the vessel?
questions.solution: After three replacements, milk = 80 × (0.9)³ = 58.32 L. Removing 20 of 80 litres keeps 3/4: 58.32 × 0.75 = 43.74 L.

questions.question: A sum amounts to ₹13,310 in 3 years and to ₹14,641 in 4 years at compound interest (annual compounding). What is the sum, in ₹?
The cost of a diamond varies as the square of its weight. A diamond worth ₹1,60,000 breaks into three pieces whose weights are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 5. What is the loss, in ₹, due to the breakage?
questions.solution: Total 'square units': 8² = 64 before, 1 + 4 + 25 = 30 after. Loss = 160000 × 34/64 = ₹85,000.

questions.question: For how many integer values of a does the equation x² − ax + 2a = 0 have both roots integers?
If x + 1/x = 3, what is the value of x⁵ + 1/x⁵?
questions.solution: Let tₙ = xⁿ + x⁻ⁿ, so tₙ₊₁ = 3tₙ − tₙ₋₁. t₀ = 2, t₁ = 3, t₂ = 7, t₃ = 18, t₄ = 47, t₅ = 123.

questions.question: How many ordered pairs of positive integers (x, y) satisfy 3x + 5y ≤ 60?
If log₂(log₃(log₄ x)) = 0, and y = log_x 2, what is 1/y?
questions.solution: log₃(log₄ x) = 1, so log₄ x = 3 and x = 64. Then y = log₆₄ 2 = 1/6, so 1/y = 6.

questions.question: A function satisfies f(x) + 2f(1/x) = 3x for all x ≠ 0. What is f(2)?
questions.solution: Substitute x → 1/x: f(1/x) + 2f(x) = 3/x. Solving the pair gives f(x) = (2/x) − x. Then f(2) = 1 − 2 = −1.

questions.question: The sum of the first n terms of a sequence is 3n² + 5n. What is the sum of its 10th, 20th and 30th terms?
questions.solution: aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ = 6n + 2. So a₁₀ + a₂₀ + a₃₀ = 62 + 122 + 182 = 366.

questions.question: Three numbers in a geometric progression have sum 26 and product 216. What is the largest of them?
questions.solution: Let the terms be a/r, a, ar. Then a³ = 216, so a = 6, and 6/r + 6 + 6r = 26 gives 3r² − 10r + 3 = 0, so r = 3 or 1/3. The terms are 2, 6, 18.

questions.question: ABCD is a square of side 12. E is the midpoint of BC and F lies on CD with CF = 3. What is the area of triangle AEF?
questions.solution: Area = square − ΔABE − ΔECF − ΔFDA = 144 − 36 − 9 − 54 = 45.

questions.question: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle whose legs are 20 and 21. What is the radius of the circle?
C is the circle x² + y² − 6x + 8y = 0. A point P moves so that the two tangents from P to C always make an angle of 60° with each other. What is the largest possible x-coordinate of P?
questions.solution: Step 1: C has centre (3, −4) and radius √(9 + 16) = 5. Step 2: if the tangents from P meet at 60°, each makes 30° with the line to the centre, so the distance from P to the centre is r / sin 30° = 10. Step 3: P lies on the circle of radius 10 about (3, −4), whose largest x-coordinate is 3 + 10 = 13.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 7^99 is divided by 2400?
How many integers from 1 to 2000 are divisible by 6 or by 10, but not by 15?
questions.solution: Multiples of 6: 333; of 10: 200; of both (30): 66. Union = 467. A number in the union is divisible by 15 exactly when it is a multiple of 30 (6 and 15 give 30; 10 and 15 give 30): 66 of them. 467 − 66 = 401.

questions.question: In how many ways can the letters of the word BALLOON be arranged so that the two L's are not together?
questions.solution: Total = 7!/(2! 2!) = 1260. With the L's together (treat LL as one letter): 6!/2! = 360. So 1260 − 360 = 900.

questions.question: Two dice are rolled. Given that the sum is at least 9, what is the probability that at least one die shows 6?

The average weight of a group of 20 is 50 kg. When two people weighing 62 kg and 70 kg leave and two new people join, the average falls by 1.5 kg. What is the average weight, in kg, of the two newcomers?
questions.solution: New total = 20 × 48.5 = 970. The remaining 18 weigh 1000 − 132 = 868. The newcomers weigh 102 kg together, an average of 51 kg.

questions.question: The population of a town rises by 20% in the first year, falls by 25% in the second, and rises by 10% in the third. If it is 59,400 at the end of three years, what was the initial population?
A sells an article to B at a 20% profit; B sells it to C at a 10% loss; C sells it to D for ₹2,646, making a 22.5% profit. What did A pay for the article, in ₹?

Two runners start together from the same point on a 400 m circular track, running in the same direction at 5 m/s and 3 m/s. After how many seconds do they meet at the starting point for the first time?
questions.solution: The faster runner returns to the start every 80 s, the slower every 400/3 s. LCM(80, 400/3) = LCM(240, 400)/3 = 1200/3 = 400 s.

questions.question: A car covers the first third of a journey at 30 km/h, the second third at 45 km/h and the last third at 90 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey, in km/h?

Pipes A and B fill a tank in 12 and 15 hours; pipe C empties it in 20 hours. All three are opened together at 6 a.m., and C is closed at 10 a.m. At what hour of the day (in 24-hour format, e.g. 15 for 3 p.m.) is the tank full?
questions.solution: Net rate with C = 5/60 + 4/60 − 3/60 = 6/60 = 1/10, so 4 hours fill 2/5. The remaining 3/5 at 9/60 per hour takes 4 hours. The tank is full at 6 + 4 + 4 = 14, i.e. 2 p.m.

questions.question: Two alloys contain gold and copper in the ratios 2 : 3 and 5 : 3. How many kg of the second must be mixed with 10 kg of the first to obtain an alloy with gold and copper in equal amounts?
questions.solution: Gold: 4 + 5x/8; copper: 6 + 3x/8. Setting them equal gives 2x/8 = 2, so x = 8 kg.

questions.question: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on a sum for 3 years at 10% per annum is ₹1,550. What is the sum, in ₹?
Let n be the least positive integer such that 180 divides 150ⁿ. If m is the least positive integer such that 150ⁿ divides 180ᵐ, what is m + n?
questions.solution: 180 = 2² × 3² × 5 and 150 = 2 × 3 × 5². Step 1: 150ⁿ = 2ⁿ3ⁿ5²ⁿ needs n ≥ 2 for both 2² and 3², so n = 2. Step 2: 150² = 2² × 3² × 5⁴ must divide 180ᵐ = 2²ᵐ3²ᵐ5ᵐ; the 5s force m ≥ 4, so m = 4. Step 3: m + n = 6.

questions.question: The average of five distinct positive integers is 20 and their median is 22. What is the largest possible value of the largest of them?
questions.solution: The sum is 100. To maximise the largest, minimise the others: 1, 2, 22, 23 total 48, leaving 52.

questions.question: The roots of x² − 6x + k = 0 are α and β, with α² − β² = 24 and α > β. What is k?
questions.solution: α + β = 6 and α² − β² = 24, so α − β = 4. Then α = 5, β = 1 and k = αβ = 5.

questions.question: How many ordered pairs of positive integers (x, y) satisfy x² − y² = 2025?
questions.solution: (x − y)(x + y) = 2025 = 3⁴ × 5². Both factors must be odd (they are, since 2025 is odd) with x − y < x + y. 2025 has 15 divisors; excluding 45 × 45 (which gives y = 0), there are 7 pairs with d < 2025/d.

questions.question: x and y are positive reals with x + 2y = 12. What is the maximum possible value of x²y?
questions.solution: Write x + 2y = x/2 + x/2 + 2y. By AM–GM, (x/2)(x/2)(2y) ≤ 4³ = 64, so x²y/2 ≤ 64 and x²y ≤ 128, with equality at x = 8, y = 2.

questions.question: If log₃ x + log₉ x + log₂₇ x = 11/2, what is x?
f(x) = (3x + 2)/(x − 3) for x ≠ 3. What is f(f(f(f(5))))?
questions.solution: f(f(x)) = x for this function: (3f + 2)/(f − 3) = (3(3x+2) + 2(x−3))/((3x+2) − 3(x−3)) = 11x/11 = x. So applying f four times returns 5.

questions.question: How many terms are common to the arithmetic progressions 4, 9, 14, …, 499 and 3, 10, 17, …, 500?
questions.solution: Common terms form an AP with difference 35. The first common term is 24 (24 = 4 + 20 = 3 + 21). The terms 24, 59, …, up to 499 number ⌊(499 − 24)/35⌋ + 1 = 13 + 1 = 14.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AB = 13, BC = 14 and CA = 15. If m is the length of the median from A to BC, what is m²?
questions.solution: By Apollonius' theorem, m² = (2b² + 2c² − a²)/4 = (450 + 338 − 196)/4 = 148.

questions.question: A ladder 25 m long leans against a vertical wall with its foot 7 m from the wall. If the top slides down 4 m, how far, in m, does the foot slide outward?
questions.solution: The original height is 24 m; the new height is 20 m. The new distance is √(625 − 400) = 15, so the foot slides 15 − 7 = 8 m.

questions.question: A rectangular sheet 44 cm × 18 cm is rolled along its longer side to form a hollow cylinder of height 18 cm. What is the volume of the cylinder, in cm³? (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.solution: Circumference 44 = 2πr gives r = 7. Volume = (22/7) × 49 × 18 = 2772.

questions.question: What are the last two digits of 3^2026?
How many positive integers less than 500 have exactly three positive divisors?
questions.solution: Exactly three divisors means n = p² for a prime p. p² < 500 needs p ≤ 22: p = 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19. That is 8 numbers.

questions.question: In how many ways can 12 identical chocolates be distributed among 4 children so that each child gets at least 2 and no child gets more than 5?
questions.solution: With yᵢ = xᵢ − 2, we need y₁ + … + y₄ = 4 with each yᵢ ≤ 3. Unrestricted: C(7,3) = 35. Subtract the 4 cases where one yᵢ = 4: 35 − 4 = 31.

questions.question: A bag holds 4 red and 6 blue balls. Balls are drawn one at a time, without replacement, until both colours have appeared. What is the expected number of draws?
questions.solution: Let D be the number of draws. D > k exactly when the first k balls are all one colour. Step 1: E[D] = Σₖ≥0 P(D > k) = 1 + Σₖ≥1 [P(first k all red) + P(first k all blue)]. Step 2: P(first k red) = C(4,k)/C(10,k) and P(first k blue) = C(6,k)/C(10,k). Step 3: red terms 4/10 + 6/45 + 4/120 + 1/210 = 0.5714…; blue terms 6/10 + 15/45 + 20/120 + 15/210 + 6/252 + 1/210 = 1.2. Step 4: E[D] = 1 + 0.5714… + 1.2 = 2.7714… = 97/35.

questions.question: If log₂x + log₄y = 4 and log₄x + log₂y = 5, what is the value of xy?
questions.solution: Write a = log₂x and b = log₂y. Since log₄ = ½ log₂, the equations are a + b/2 = 4 and a/2 + b = 5, i.e. 2a + b = 8 and a + 2b = 10. So a = 2 and b = 4, giving x = 4, y = 16 and xy = 64.

questions.question: How many integers n satisfy 1 < log₂(log₃ n) < 2?
questions.solution: 1 < log₂(log₃ n) < 2 means 2 < log₃ n < 4, i.e. 9 < n < 81. The integers are 10, 11, …, 80, which is 71 integers.

questions.question: What is the product of all real values of x for which x^(log₁₀x) = 100x?
questions.solution: Take log₁₀ of both sides and write t = log₁₀x: t·t = 2 + t, so t² − t − 2 = 0 and t = 2 or t = −1. Then x = 100 or x = 1/10 (both positive, so both valid), and the product is 100 × 1/10 = 10.

questions.question: If log₁₂18 = a, then log₂₄16 equals
Let f(x) = x/(1 + x) for x > 0, and let fⁿ denote f applied n times (so f²(x) = f(f(x))). What is f¹⁰(1)?
questions.solution: f(f(x)) = (x/(1 + x))/(1 + x/(1 + x)) = x/(1 + 2x), and in general fⁿ(x) = x/(1 + nx), as each step adds x to the denominator. So f¹⁰(1) = 1/(1 + 10) = 1/11.

questions.question: How many functions f from {1, 2, 3, 4} to itself satisfy f(f(x)) = x for every x in the set?
questions.solution: Such an f pairs the elements up and fixes the rest (any element not fixed is swapped with its partner). No swaps: 1 function. Exactly one swapped pair: C(4,2) = 6. Two swapped pairs: 3. Total = 1 + 6 + 3 = 10.

questions.question: For real x, let g(x) = min(2x + 1, x + 4, 7 − x). What is the largest value g(x) can take?
questions.solution: 7 − x falls as x grows while the other two rise, so the maximum of the minimum is where 7 − x meets the smaller rising line. 2x + 1 = 7 − x at x = 2, where both equal 5 and x + 4 = 6 is larger. (Where x + 4 = 7 − x, at x = 1.5, 2x + 1 is only 4.) So the largest value is 5, at x = 2.

questions.question: Section A has 30 students with an average score of 62, and Section B has 45 students with an average of 58. Five students move from A to B, after which A's average rises to 63. What is B's new average?
questions.solution: The five movers' total = 30 × 62 − 25 × 63 = 1860 − 1575 = 285. B's new total = 45 × 58 + 285 = 2610 + 285 = 2895 for 50 students, so its average is 2895/50 = 57.9.

questions.question: A, B and C start a business with capitals in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. After 4 months A doubles his capital, and after 6 months C withdraws half of hers. B's capital is unchanged. Out of a year-end profit of ₹15,300, what is C's share (in ₹)?
In how many ways can 12 be written as a sum of three different positive integers, if the order of the terms does not matter?

A and B take turns, A first. On each of A's turns A rolls a fair die and wins on a six; on each of B's turns B tosses a fair coin and wins on heads. They continue until someone wins. What is the probability that A wins?
questions.solution: A round in which nobody wins has probability (5/6)(1/2) = 5/12. A wins on the first turn of a round with probability 1/6, so P(A) = (1/6)(1 + 5/12 + (5/12)² + …) = (1/6)/(7/12) = 2/7.

questions.question: In a geometric progression with positive terms, the sum of the first three terms is 26 and the sum of the next three terms is 702. What is the fifth term?
questions.solution: The next three terms are the first three multiplied by r³, so r³ = 702/26 = 27 and r = 3. Then a(1 + 3 + 9) = 26 gives a = 2, and the fifth term is 2 × 3⁴ = 162.

questions.question: What is the value of 1×2 + 2×3 + 3×4 + … + 20×21?
A rectangular lawn is 60 m by 40 m. A path of uniform width runs inside it along all four edges, and the path's area is 736 m². What is the width of the path (in m)?
questions.solution: The grass left is (60 − 2w)(40 − 2w) = 2400 − 736 = 1664. Expanding, 4w² − 200w + 2400 = 1664, i.e. w² − 50w + 184 = 0, so w = (50 ± 42)/2 = 4 or 46. The width must be under 20 m, so w = 4.

questions.question: How many non-congruent triangles with integer side lengths have a perimeter of 20?
What is the remainder when 1! + 2! + 3! + … + 100! is divided by 12?
questions.solution: From 4! = 24 onwards every factorial is a multiple of 12, so only 1! + 2! + 3! = 1 + 2 + 6 = 9 matters. The remainder is 9.

questions.question: How many integers from 1 to 1000 are perfect squares or perfect cubes (or both)?
questions.solution: Squares: 1², …, 31² (32² = 1024 is too big), so 31. Cubes: 1³, …, 10³, so 10. Both means sixth powers: 1, 64 and 729, so 3. Total = 31 + 10 − 3 = 38.

questions.question: The roots of x² − px + q = 0 are two consecutive integers. What is the value of p² − 4q?
questions.solution: If the roots are n and n + 1, then p = 2n + 1 and q = n(n + 1). So p² − 4q = 4n² + 4n + 1 − 4n² − 4n = 1. (p² − 4q is also the square of the difference of the roots, which is 1² = 1.)

questions.question: How many real numbers x satisfy x² − 5|x| + 6 = 0?
questions.solution: Since x² = |x|², the equation is |x|² − 5|x| + 6 = 0, so |x| = 2 or |x| = 3. That gives x = ±2 and ±3: 4 solutions.

questions.question: x and y are positive real numbers with x + y = 10. What is the smallest possible value of (1 + 1/x)(1 + 1/y)?
questions.solution: (1 + 1/x)(1 + 1/y) = 1 + 1/x + 1/y + 1/(xy) = 1 + (x + y + 1)/(xy) = 1 + 11/(xy). This is smallest when xy is largest, and with x + y = 10 the largest product is 5 × 5 = 25. So the minimum is 1 + 11/25 = 36/25 = 1.44.

questions.question: Three vertices of a regular octagon are chosen to form a triangle. In how many ways can this be done so that no side of the triangle is a side of the octagon?
questions.solution: Count choices of 3 vertices with no two adjacent. Total C(8,3) = 56. With at least one adjacent pair: a pair of adjacent vertices can be chosen in 8 ways and the third vertex in 6 ways, but the 8 triangles made of three consecutive vertices are counted twice, so 8 × 6 − 8 = 40. Answer = 56 − 40 = 16.

questions.question: What is the value of log₃5 × log₂₅27?
questions.solution: log₃5 × log₂₅27 = (log 5/log 3) × (3 log 3/2 log 5) = 3/2.

questions.question: The average of 20 numbers is 0. At most how many of them can be greater than 0?
questions.solution: Not all 20 can be positive, because then the sum would be positive. 19 can be: take nineteen 1s and one −19, whose sum is 0. So the answer is 19.

questions.question: The 3rd, 5th and 9th terms of a non-constant arithmetic progression are, in that order, three consecutive terms of a geometric progression. What is the common ratio of the geometric progression?
questions.solution: With first term a and difference d ≠ 0: (a + 4d)² = (a + 2d)(a + 8d). Expanding, a² + 8ad + 16d² = a² + 10ad + 16d², so 2ad = 0 and a = 0. The three terms are 2d, 4d and 8d, so the ratio is 2.

questions.question: A positive divisor of 720 is chosen at random, all divisors being equally likely. What is the probability that it is a multiple of 12?
questions.solution: 720 = 2⁴ × 3² × 5 has 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 divisors. A multiple of 12 = 2² × 3 needs the power of 2 to be 2, 3 or 4 (3 ways), the power of 3 to be 1 or 2 (2 ways) and any power of 5 (2 ways): 12 divisors. Probability = 12/30 = 2/5.

questions.question: Two cyclists start at the same time from towns 300 km apart and ride towards each other at 40 km/h and 60 km/h. A drone starts with the first cyclist and flies at 80 km/h back and forth between the two, turning instantly, until the cyclists meet. How many km does the drone fly?
questions.solution: The cyclists close the gap at 40 + 60 = 100 km/h, so they meet after 300/100 = 3 hours. The drone flies the whole 3 hours at 80 km/h, i.e. 240 km. There is no need to add up the individual trips.

questions.question: Two parallel chords of a circle have lengths 16 cm and 30 cm and lie on opposite sides of the centre, 23 cm apart. What is the radius of the circle (in cm)?
questions.solution: Let the 16 cm chord be a cm from the centre and the 30 cm chord (23 − a) cm away. Then r² = 8² + a² = 15² + (23 − a)². So 64 + a² = 225 + 529 − 46a + a², giving 46a = 690 and a = 15. r² = 64 + 225 = 289, so r = 17.

questions.question: A batsman scores 87 runs in an innings and his batting average goes up by 3. In his very next innings he scores 33 and his average falls by 2. How many innings had he played before the innings in which he scored 87?
questions.solution: Let him have played n innings with average a. After 87: (na + 87)/(n + 1) = a + 3, so 87 = a + 3n + 3, i.e. a = 84 − 3n. After 33 the average is a + 1 over n + 2 innings: (n + 1)(a + 3) + 33 = (n + 2)(a + 1), which simplifies to 33 = a − 2n − 1, i.e. a = 2n + 34. So 84 − 3n = 2n + 34, giving n = 10 (and a = 54). Check: 540 + 87 = 627 = 11 × 57; 627 + 33 = 660 = 12 × 55.

questions.question: The integers 1, 2, 3, …, n are written on a board and one of them is erased. The average of the numbers left is 35 47/69. Which number was erased?
